content.text: In a metal the outer-shell electrons detach and wander through the whole lattice: positive ions held in a regular array by electrostatic attraction to this surrounding pool of delocalised electrons. That one picture explains the property set - conduction (the delocalised electrons drift when a potential is applied), malleability (layers of ions slide without shattering the attraction), and high melting points (the attraction runs through the entire lattice).
